test_cases.title: OSPF Basic Full Adjacency Establishment
test_cases.objective: Verify that two OSPF routers on a point-to-point link can establish a full adjacency through the complete state machine progression from Down to Full.

steps.description: Initialize the device test environment with two routers connected via a point-to-point link, both configured in OSPF Area 0.
Enable OSPF on both router interfaces with matching HelloInterval (10s) and DeadInterval (40s).
Wait for Hello packets to be exchanged between routers.
steps.expected_result: Both routers transition from Down to Init state upon receiving HelloReceived event.

steps.description: Verify that each router sees itself listed in the neighbor's Hello packet.
steps.expected_result: TwoWayReceived event triggers transition to ExStart. DD negotiation begins.

steps.description: Monitor Database Description exchange and LS Request/Update exchanges.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor state progresses through Exchange to Loading and reaches Full.

test_cases.title: OSPF DROther Neighbor Stays in TwoWay
test_cases.objective: Verify that two DROther routers on a broadcast network do not form a full adjacency and remain in TwoWay state.

steps.description: Initialize the test environment with three routers on a broadcast segment, all in OSPF Area 0.
Configure Router A with priority 0 and Router B with priority 0, ensuring neither becomes DR or BDR.
Enable OSPF and allow DR election to complete.
steps.expected_result: Neither Router A nor Router B is elected DR or BDR.

steps.description: Observe neighbor state between Router A and Router B.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor state between the two DROther routers reaches TwoWay and does not advance to ExStart.

test_cases.title: OSPF Link Failure During Exchange
test_cases.objective: Verify that a link-layer failure during database exchange correctly resets the neighbor to Down state via the LLDown event.

steps.description: Initialize the test environment with two routers connected via a point-to-point link in OSPF Area 0.
Enable OSPF and wait for neighbor state to reach Exchange.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor state reaches Exchange after DD negotiation.

steps.description: Simulate link-layer failure by shutting down the physical interface on one router.
steps.expected_result: LLDown event is generated; neighbor state immediately transitions to Down.

steps.description: Verify that all neighbor data structures are cleared.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor entry is removed from the neighbor table.

test_cases.title: OSPF Inactivity Timer Expiry During Loading
test_cases.objective: Verify that inactivity timer expiry during Loading state correctly resets the neighbor to Down state.

steps.description: Initialize the test environment with two routers on a point-to-point link in OSPF Area 0.
Enable OSPF and wait for neighbor state to reach Loading.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor state progresses to Loading with pending LS Requests.

steps.description: Block Hello packets from the neighbor using an ACL filter to prevent Inactivity Timer refresh.
steps.expected_result: Hello packets from the neighbor are dropped; Inactivity Timer is not reset.

steps.description: Wait for the DeadInterval (40 seconds) to expire.
steps.expected_result: InactivityTimer event fires; neighbor transitions to Down state.

steps.description: Verify neighbor data structures are cleaned up.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor is removed from the neighbor table and routing table entries via this neighbor are purged.

test_cases.title: OSPF OneWay Event from TwoWay State
test_cases.objective: Verify that receiving a Hello without the local router ID listed causes transition from TwoWay back to Init via the OneWay event.

steps.description: Initialize the test environment with two DROther routers on a broadcast segment in OSPF Area 0.
Enable OSPF and wait for neighbor state to reach TwoWay.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor state reaches TwoWay as no adjacency is needed between DROthers.

steps.description: Send a crafted Hello packet from the tester that does not include the DUT router ID in the neighbor list.
steps.expected_result: DUT generates OneWay event; neighbor state transitions from TwoWay to Init.

steps.description: Verify that neighbor state is Init.
steps.expected_result: Neighbor state shows Init in the neighbor table.
